asks: Asks for at least one, preferably two, more electoral districts for Edmonton, and opposes rural-urban hybrid ridings (two webform entries about Edmonton-Rutherford).
Former MLA is pleased with the interim map overall, asks the commission to keep hybrid ridings sparing or reduce them, and cautions against treating Edmonton's core as hollowed out.

quote: My riding included Spruce Grove, approximately a third of St Albert, the Alexander First Nation, and the rural land in between.
note: Named as her former hybrid riding (Spruce Grove-St. Albert, 2015-2019) to illustrate the general burden of hybrids; no request about St. Albert's districts.

asks: Asks the commission to adopt Interim Option B, an Okotoks-Diamond Valley district with no part of Calgary.

Asks the commission to retain the Lesser Slave Lake riding; failing that, to keep Big Lakes County whole and attach it to Peace River-Notley.

quote: the proposed elimination of the Lesser Slave Lake riding fails the effective representation test set out in the Electoral Boundaries Commission Act. It recommends retaining the LSL riding.
note: Fallback if the riding cannot be kept: all of Big Lakes County, whole, in Peace River-Notley (p. 42).

asks: Asks the commission to adopt the interim Edmonton-Beverly-Clareview boundaries exactly as proposed.

note: Header: about 77 - Red Deer-North. Asks to keep the 2023 boundaries and believes the proposal adds rural area. Argues against mixing urban and rural in the riding in general ('may not be properly represented if the areas are mixed'); the four-way plan is not named, so the rejection is recorded as R3, not R2.

asks: Asks the commission to reconsider swapping Heritage Hills out of Strathcona-Sherwood Park for Beaumont.
Asks the commission to keep the 2023 Strathcona-Sherwood Park boundaries and not add parts of Beaumont and Leduc County (template letter).
Opposes swapping Heritage Hills for Beaumont in Strathcona-Sherwood Park; suggests adding Tofield if population is needed.
Federation of Calgary Communities thanks the commission for two more Calgary seats and asks it to preserve Calgary's urban integrity rather than create the three interim Calgary hybrids.
Finds the interim Calgary-Acadia reasonable and asks that the Manchester neighbourhood stay in it.
Tofield residents ask to be moved from the Camrose division into Strathcona-Sherwood Park.
Asks the commission to keep southeast Edmonton's seats close to the interim map, inside the city, and to add at least one more Edmonton seat.
Supports the interim Calgary-Edgemont boundaries and asks for clear, local polling stations.
Supports the interim Edmonton-Whitemud boundaries and the avoidance of hybrids, and asks for one more Edmonton seat.
Supports the interim Calgary-Edgemont boundaries, urges the commission to resist hybrid ridings, and suggests an additional Calgary riding for growth.
Supports interim Edmonton-Decore in the main, asks the commission to avoid making Edmonton-Manning a rural-urban hybrid and to keep urban boundaries clear.

note: Tentative suggestion that Olds (or Blackfalds) could be added to the Innisfail riding; too tentative and too thin to code as a want (rule 17). If coded it would be O9.
Sylvan Lake / Innisfail letter of the kind the codebook says to record as a mention with no want; Red Deer is not named and nothing is said about a town sharing a district with the city.

asks: MLA asks that polls 43, 44 and 45 be moved from Morinville-St. Albert into the St. Albert riding.

quote: I am writing to suggest the relocation of polling sites 43, 44, and 45 from the Morinville-St. Albert riding to the St. Albert riding.
note: Header: about 83 - St. Albert-Sturgeon. Moves three polls in an older part of St. Albert out of the hybrid into the city district; which map does so depends on where the polls lie.

asks: Asks the commission to keep its interim recommendation of two urban Lethbridge ridings and not split the city into four urban-rural hybrids.

quote: Splitting Lethbridge into four urban-rural hybrid electoral divisions, in my opinion, would not make good sense.
note: Voter in Lethbridge-East. Also: 'I hope the recommendations from this Interim Report will be maintained'. Rejects the four-way split proposed in other submissions.

asks: Asks that Edmonton-Riverview keep its existing boundaries rather than be merged into Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview.
Supports the interim Edmonton-North West boundaries, including the addition of Calder.
Thanks the commission for the Edmonton seat and asks that part of St. Albert join Edmonton-North West or Edmonton-West Henday instead of the St. Albert-Sturgeon hybrid.

quote: I take issue with the choice to continue including part of St. Albert in the proposed St.Albert-Sturgeon division. I believe that it would make much more sense to have a southern section of St.Albert be part of Edmonton-North West
note: Edmonton-North West resident. Wants part of St. Albert joined to an Edmonton riding (Edmonton-North West or Edmonton-West Henday) instead of the city-county hybrid; on no map. Rejection is of the hybrid half of the long-standing pattern.

asks: Asks that no boundaries be changed and that Edmonton-Riverview remain.
Supports Edmonton-Glenora-Riverview, prefers map option B because it uses hybrids more sparingly, and asks for no more than one hybrid riding per big city.

quote: It makes less difference to representation if Edmonton has 21 or 22 ridings than if Airdrie has 1 or 2.
note: Airdrie named only as an example of a small city (rule 6).

quote: Even the old riding combining St. Albert and northwest Edmonton, two urban areas, has been abandoned, to give Edmonton its own exclusive ridings.
note: St. Albert named only as an example from the federal map (rule 6).

asks: MD of Bighorn resident supports the interim Banff-Jasper division, including all Stoney reserves in one riding and the removal of Springbank and Elbow Valley.

note: Airdrie named only as a place the writer once worked ('in Okotoks and Airdrie and Calgary'). The letter supports interim Banff-Jasper with all Stoney reserves in one riding but never speaks of Rocky Mountain House or Clearwater County, so no RMH-B line.

asks: Asks that Springbank be placed in Calgary-Bow rather than with Cochrane or Canmore.

quote: the residents of Springbank would be far better served by being included within the Calgary Bow electoral district rather than being aligned with Cochrane or Canmore
note: Calgary-Bow resident asks that Springbank go to Calgary-Bow, which would take Springbank out of the interim Cochrane-Springbank district. Speaks from Springbank's side and says nothing of what Cochrane should be joined to, so no want or rejects is recorded (rule 17); a broader reading would be rejects C1.

asks: Asks the commission to leave Strathcona-Sherwood Park as it is, without Beaumont and with Heritage Hills.
Asks that Springbank be included in Calgary-Bow.

quote: I am against the elimination of the Lesser Slave Lake constituency based on the lack of population.
note: Big Lakes County resident. Proposes adding the Swan Hills area to raise the population, which both final maps do.

asks: Asks that Strathcona-Sherwood Park keep Heritage Hills and not take in Beaumont; suggests Tofield if population is needed.

note: Lacombe County resident; header: about 67 - Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House. Argues against the Lacombe-Rocky Mountain House pairing itself, which is the interim riding (W3) and also the essence of the majority's Lacombe-Clearwater (W2). No arrangement is asked for; nothing on dividing Clearwater County.

note: Coalhurst resident. Also thanks the commission for not merging her rural area with urban ridings ('any of the hybrid ridings suggested'), a preference rather than an argued rejection of L2. asks: Asks that the Bremner growth area be added to Strathcona-Sherwood Park in place of Beaumont, following Strathcona County's boundaries.

note: MLA for Edmonton-Rutherford welcomes the interim Mackenzie seat as a step for Indigenous representation. Lesser Slave Lake is not named; Mackenzie is the interim district that replaces it, so support for it is coded as K2 at direction level. A narrower reading is mention only.

asks: Asks the commission not to split Beaumont and put half of it with Strathcona.

note: Essay on gerrymandering; cites the merger as an example of dissolved or merged ridings and criticises larger rural ridings in general, but makes no stated request about Lesser Slave Lake (rule 17). A broader reading would be rejects K2.
